title: Technical Q&A, senior software engineer, weak answers

questions.text: How would you find the cause of a memory leak in a long running service?
How do you decide when to add a cache?
Explain how a database index works.
How would you design a retry policy for calls between services?
Explain the CAP theorem in plain words.
How would you roll out a risky schema change?

persona.pushback_style: asks for the tools and the specific case

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Hi Bertrand, thanks for joining. I'm Fiona, an engineer on the platform team. This is a thirty minute technical conversation with spoken questions and no coding.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi Fiona, thank you.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What are you working on at the moment?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I am a senior developer on a web application. Mostly features and bug fixes.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Okay. I'll ask three or four questions about debugging and design, and then leave time for yours.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How would you find the cause of a memory leak in a long running service?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would look at the logs and monitor the memory. Then I would restart the service if it gets too high. Maybe look at the code to see where the leak is.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What tools would you use to see which objects are growing?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A profiler, I guess. There are profiler tools that show memory. I would use one of those and look for the problem.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Walk me through what you did the last time you had a leak.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Last time we restarted it every night. It was a quick fix.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you decide when to add a cache?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: When the application is slow. Caching makes things faster, so you cache the data that is used a lot. Redis is good for that.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Explain how a database index works.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: An index is like a shortcut to the data. It makes queries and also writes faster, because the data is organized. You should index every column.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What does an index cost? Think about writes and storage.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Storage a bit. I do not think writes are affected much. It is generally worth it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Thanks. What questions do you have for me?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: What does a senior engineer own on your team?

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: A senior engineer owns a service end to end, mentors two engineers, and writes the design review for large changes.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That's our time. Thanks Bertrand, the recruiter will contact you within a week.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thank you, Fiona.

notes: Weak for senior: short generic answers, tool names without detail, one wrong claim about indexes, no numbers, no examples.
